items.stem: How does Synnduit compose its parts (services, sinks, feeds)?

options.text: Via Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection registrations in a startup file
Via MEF — attribute-driven discovery of parts, with no central registration list
By reading a JSON list of class names
Every class is new-ed up manually in Main()

items.explanation: Synnduit uses MEF: classes are decorated with attributes and discovered, rather than registered in a container.

misconceptions.a: This is the trap for experienced DI devs — there is no services.Add... registration to find; MEF discovers attributed parts.

options.text: This is the constructor MEF should use, injecting the imported services into its parameters
To run this constructor on a background thread
This class exports itself as a service

items.explanation: [ImportingConstructor] marks the constructor MEF uses for injection — the MEF counterpart to the container-resolved constructor.

misconceptions.d: That's [Export]; [ImportingConstructor] is about receiving imports, not publishing one.

items.stem: Which attribute publishes a class as the implementation of a service contract so other parts can import it?
items.explanation: [Export(typeof(IService))] declares the class as the export for that contract; importers receive it.

misconceptions.a: [Sink] marks a connector part for discovery, not a service export.

items.stem: In MEF terms, `[PartCreationPolicy(CreationPolicy.Shared)]` on an [Export]ed service is most like which Microsoft.Extensions.DI concept?
items.explanation: CreationPolicy.Shared yields a single shared instance — analogous to a singleton registration.

misconceptions.a: Transient corresponds to CreationPolicy.NonShared, not Shared.

items.stem: A strong DI developer greps the Synnduit codebase for `services.AddSingleton` and finds nothing, then concludes the service isn't wired up. What did they miss, and how does the sink actually reach its service?
rubric: Synnduit uses MEF, not the Microsoft.Extensions.DI container — there is no AddSingleton/AddScoped registration
The service is published with [Export] (+ [PartCreationPolicy(Shared)]) and discovered by MEF
The sink receives it through its [ImportingConstructor]
items.sampleAnswer: They assumed the standard DI container; Synnduit uses MEF, so there's no services.Add... call. The service is wired up by attributes: it's marked [Export(typeof(ITeamSiteWebPartService))] (and [PartCreationPolicy(CreationPolicy.Shared)] for a single instance), MEF discovers it, and injects it into the sink's [ImportingConstructor].
